cleanIntro:
This guide follows Auto-Ordnance's Thompson Semi-Auto Models owner's manual (041610KAP), which does not name the Thompson T1SB50DH, so check your variant against it. Auto-Ordnance prints one owner's manual for its Thompson semi-auto models. It names the T1SB, the 10.5-inch short-barrel 1927A-1, and states that the takedown is the same for every Thompson semi-auto; Auto-Ordnance lists the T1SB50DH beside the T1SB as the same short-barrel rifle, sold with a horizontal foregrip, a 50-round drum and a 20-round stick magazine. Every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it.

The strip is unusual: the frame slides off the back of the receiver, and the recoil spring guide is under spring tension when it comes out. Keep a 1/8-inch flat-blade screwdriver to hand before you start.

steps.title: Know what you are holding
steps.action: This guide follows Auto-Ordnance's Thompson Semi-Auto Models owner's manual (041610KAP), which does not name the Thompson T1SB50DH, so check your variant against it. Every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it; where the book singles out one model, that text is not applied here.
steps.prose: The book lists the Thompson models it covers on its contents page: the T1, T5, T1SB, TM1 / TM1C, M1SB and T1-C. The T1SB50DH is not in that list. The book's short-barrel nomenclature page labels the T1SB as a 1927A-1 and the M1SB as an M1, and the two patterns differ: the M1 models take the bolt handle out of the side of the receiver and will not accept a drum magazine. If your rifle has a side bolt handle or no drum slots, it is not the rifle this guide is written for.
steps.quote: Takedown procedures for all Thompson semi-autos are the same.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL TO BE USED FOR THOMPSON SEMI-AUTO MODELS — 041610KAP (code printed on the back cover beneath the copyright line, p.28) — Disassembly of the Semi-Auto Thompson for Routine Cleaning, p.15

steps.title: Stick magazine out, then look in the chamber
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction and fingers outside the trigger guard. Push up on the magazine catch and pull the stick magazine down and out. Taking the magazine out does not unload the rifle. A round can still be sitting in the chamber, so you check the chamber next.
steps.quote:
2. Push up on the magazine catch and remove the magazine.
WARNING: EVEN THOUGH THE MAGAZINE HAS BEEN REMOVED A CARTRIDGE REMAINING IN THE CHAMBER CAN STILL BE FIRED. ALWAYS VISUALLY CHECK THE CHAMBER.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL TO BE USED FOR THOMPSON SEMI-AUTO MODELS — 041610KAP (code printed on the back cover beneath the copyright line, p.28) — Loading and Firing the Thompson: To Unload the Thompson, p.15

steps.title: Drum fitted: bolt locked back, drum slid out to the left
steps.action: If the 50-round drum is in, it does not drop out like the stick magazine. The bolt has to be locked back first, and the bolt closes on its own after the last round from a drum. Once the bolt is locked back, push up on the magazine catch and slide the drum out of its slots to the left side of the rifle. Do not try to pull it straight down like a stick magazine.
steps.aside: While pushing up on the magazine catch the drum magazine can be slid out of the slots from the left side of the firearm.
steps.quote: 5. To insert or remove the drum magazine from the firearm, the bolt must be locked back. Please refer to page 9 under “Operation of the Bolt Lock.”
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL TO BE USED FOR THOMPSON SEMI-AUTO MODELS — 041610KAP (code printed on the back cover beneath the copyright line, p.28) — Magazines: Stick Magazine and Drum Magazines, step 5, p.13

steps.title: Bolt back, chamber empty
steps.action: Pull the bolt handle all the way to the rear. That extracts and ejects any round in the chamber. The book's safety page warns against drawing the bolt with the safety on, so do it with the lever forward on FIRE and your finger off the trigger. Then look into the chamber and confirm it is empty, and put the safety back on SAFE. In the book's terms, a safe rifle has the bolt open, the chamber and magazine empty and the safety on.
steps.quote:
3. Pull the bolt handle all the way to the rear, extracting and ejecting the cartridge in the chamber.
4. Visually confirm the chamber is empty. A safe rifle is one in which the bolt is open and the chamber and magazine are empty and safety is on.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL TO BE USED FOR THOMPSON SEMI-AUTO MODELS — 041610KAP (code printed on the back cover beneath the copyright line, p.28) — Loading and Firing the Thompson: To Unload the Thompson, p.15
steps.warn: DO NOT PULL BOLT BACK WITH SAFETY ON OR DAMAGE TO THE FIRING PIN MAY RESULT AS WELL AS PERSONAL INJURY.

steps.title: Bolt forward, safety on FIRE before you start
steps.action: Check the chamber once more. Then set the rifle up the way the book wants it before the frame comes off: bolt forward, firing pin in its fired position, and the safety lever rotated forward to FIRE. This is the opposite of where the safety sat while you were clearing, and the order matters. The frame will not come off the way the book describes unless the action is in this state.
steps.quote: 2. Confirm once again that the rifle is unloaded by visually checking the chamber. Before disassembly the bolt should be in the forward position, firing pin in the fired position and the safety lever in the “FIRE” position.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL TO BE USED FOR THOMPSON SEMI-AUTO MODELS — 041610KAP (code printed on the back cover beneath the copyright line, p.28) — Disassembly of the Semi-Auto Thompson for Routine Cleaning, step 2, p.15

steps.title: Frame latch button pressed, frame drawn back
steps.action: Turn the rifle upside down. Using a flat-blade screwdriver with a 1/8-inch blade, press in the frame latch button at the rear underside of the receiver, and at the same time pull the frame to the rear. A new rifle can be tight here. Once the frame has moved past the button you can take the screwdriver away and keep pulling.
steps.quote: 3. With the firearm upside down and using a flat-blade screwdriver with a 1/8” width blade depress the frame latch button in the rear bottom portion of the receiver. (See PICTURE #1) At the same time pull the frame to the rear (new guns may be tight).
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL TO BE USED FOR THOMPSON SEMI-AUTO MODELS — 041610KAP (code printed on the back cover beneath the copyright line, p.28) — Disassembly of the Semi-Auto Thompson for Routine Cleaning, step 3, p.15

steps.title: Button pressed a second time, frame off
steps.action: About halfway back, the frame catches on the latch button again. Press the button in with the same screwdriver a second time and slide the frame the rest of the way off the receiver. The button can drop out of the receiver once the frame is off. Work over a bench so you do not lose it.
steps.aside: Care should be taken not to misplace the frame latch button should it drop out of the receiver.
steps.quote: About half way back the frame latch button will catch on the frame. Using the same flat-blade screwdriver depress the frame latch button again and remove the frame the rest of the way off the receiver.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL TO BE USED FOR THOMPSON SEMI-AUTO MODELS — 041610KAP (code printed on the back cover beneath the copyright line, p.28) — Disassembly of the Semi-Auto Thompson for Routine Cleaning, step 3, p.15

steps.title: Recoil spring guide and springs lifted out
steps.action: With the receiver still upside down, pull the recoil spring guide and its two springs up and out. The guide is under spring tension. Use the screwdriver to take pressure off it before lifting, and keep it covered as it clears the receiver. If it gets away from you, it springs out.
steps.quote: 4. While the receiver is still upside down, the internal parts of the receiver can be removed by pulling up on the recoil spring guide and springs. (See PICTURE #3) It may be helpful to use the flat-blade screwdriver to take pressure off the recoil spring guide before lifting the recoil spring guide out of the receiver.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL TO BE USED FOR THOMPSON SEMI-AUTO MODELS — 041610KAP (code printed on the back cover beneath the copyright line, p.28) — Disassembly of the Semi-Auto Thompson for Routine Cleaning, step 4, p.16
steps.warn: The recoil spring guide is under spring tension so care should be taken when the spring guide clears the receiver.

steps.title: Firing pin pilot and spring out the back
steps.action: With the recoil spring guide out, the firing pin pilot and its spring come out of the hole in the rear of the receiver. Keep the pilot and spring together. On reassembly the spring goes back partly into the rear of the bolt, and the pilot has to line up with a cut-out in the recoil spring guide.
steps.quote: After removing the recoil spring guide and springs the firing pin pilot and spring will come out of the hole in the rear of the receiver.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL TO BE USED FOR THOMPSON SEMI-AUTO MODELS — 041610KAP (code printed on the back cover beneath the copyright line, p.28) — Disassembly of the Semi-Auto Thompson for Routine Cleaning, step 4, p.16

steps.title: Muzzle up, hammer slides free, bolt handle out the top
steps.action: Hold the bolt forward, keep the rifle upside down, and tip the muzzle up so the hammer slides free of the bolt handle. Then lift the bolt handle out of its hole in the top of the receiver. The book's side-mounted handle belongs to the M1 models. On this 1927A-1 pattern rifle the handle comes out of the top.
steps.quote: 5. Holding the bolt forward with the firearm upside down point the muzzle upwards so that the hammer slides free of the bolt handle. Remove the bolt handle from the hole in the top of the receiver or from the side on the M1.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL TO BE USED FOR THOMPSON SEMI-AUTO MODELS — 041610KAP (code printed on the back cover beneath the copyright line, p.28) — Disassembly of the Semi-Auto Thompson for Routine Cleaning, step 5, p.16

steps.title: Bolt slid to the rear and lifted out
steps.action: With the handle out, slide the bolt all the way to the rear of the receiver and lift it clear. It only lifts out at the end of its travel. If it will not come up, it is not far enough back.
steps.quote: The bolt can now be removed from the receiver by sliding the bolt all the way to the rear and lifting it clear of the receiver.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL TO BE USED FOR THOMPSON SEMI-AUTO MODELS — 041610KAP (code printed on the back cover beneath the copyright line, p.28) — Disassembly of the Semi-Auto Thompson for Routine Cleaning, step 5, p.16

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, recoil spring guide and springs, firing pin pilot and spring, bolt handle and bolt are all out of the receiver. That is as far as Auto-Ordnance takes the rifle for routine cleaning. The book stops at the frame, and it warns separately that removing the pivot plate with the frame on the receiver voids the warranty. Oil the pivot points and the bolt-to-receiver sliding surfaces lightly as you clean.
steps.quote: 6. Further disassembly of the frame is not normally required for routine cleaning. A light coat of oil on pivot points and sliding surfaces between the bolt and receiver is recommended.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL TO BE USED FOR THOMPSON SEMI-AUTO MODELS — 041610KAP (code printed on the back cover beneath the copyright line, p.28) — Disassembly of the Semi-Auto Thompson for Routine Cleaning, step 6, p.16
steps.warn: WARRANTY IS VOIDED IF PIVOT PLATE IS REMOVED WITH FRAME ON RECEIVER.

deepAbsentReason: The book's field strip ends at step 6 on p.16: 'Further disassembly of the frame is not normally required for routine cleaning.' It publishes no deeper procedure for the rifle — the frame, the pivot plate and the bolt's own parts are never taken down — and it carries the separate warning 'WARRANTY IS VOIDED IF PIVOT PLATE IS REMOVED WITH FRAME ON RECEIVER.' (p.16). The only other teardowns in the book are the stick magazine (p.18) and the drum's loading procedure (pp.12-13), which are magazines, not a deeper clean of the rifle.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Run a patch wetted with a quality gun cleaning solution through the bore several times
Run a wetted bristle brush back and forth the full length of the bore and the chamber
Dry patches through the bore, then examine it
Grease left in the chamber interferes with feeding, so get it out
Finish with a dry patch, then a very lightly oiled patch

cleaning.name: BOLT, RECEIVER & FRAME
tasks: Remove powder residue from every part of the mechanism with solvent on a clean patch or bristle brush
Wipe all surfaces clean, then wipe them with a very lightly oiled cloth
A light coat of oil on the pivot points and the sliding surfaces between bolt and receiver
Do not remove the pivot plate with the frame on the receiver, which voids the warranty

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Stick magazine: load one round, press it down and let go; it must snap fully up to the feeding position
If cleaning does not restore the spring tension, do not use that magazine
The stick magazine spring is under tension when the baseplate slides off
Do not open a drum's cover while it is loaded and the rotor is under tension
Never use a damaged, non-standard or improperly assembled magazine

cleaning.name: OIL — LIGHT
tasks: Only a light application of oil is needed for lubrication and rust protection
Excess oil attracts dust and dirt and can congeal in cold weather
Do not spray or apply lubricant directly on ammunition
Never fire with oil, grease or anything else partly obstructing the bore

reassembly: Put the bolt into the rear of the receiver and slide it forward through the hole in the front of the receiver.
Line up the holes in the bolt and the receiver and drop the bolt handle into the top of the receiver; with the receiver upside down, put the hammer into the hole in the rear of the bolt.
Put the firing pin pilot and its spring into the hole in the rear of the receiver, with the spring going partly into the rear of the bolt.

With the bolt fully forward, put the two recoil springs into the two holes in the top rear of the bolt and push the guide forward against the spring tension; keep control of it, because it can slip and fly out.

Hold the back of the firing pin pilot so its small-diameter portion lines up with the cut-out in the recoil spring guide, then press the guide fully down onto the pilot until it sits flush with the receiver.
With the receiver upside down, line the frame slots up on the rear of the receiver rails and push the frame fully on until it passes the frame latch button and locks.
fncheck: With the rifle empty and pointed somewhere safe, check the frame is locked on and will not slide back without the latch button being pressed. Rotate the safety lever fully rearward to SAFE and fully forward to FIRE and confirm it goes all the way each time. With the safety on FIRE, draw the bolt fully back and push up on the trip lever at the top of the magazine guide rails, then let the bolt forward until it locks in place. The bolt lock is only a convenience for changing magazines and cleaning, not a safety, so confirm it holds the bolt and then release it under control, keeping your fingers clear of the bolt's path.
